summary: SatelliFarm is a web platform designed to support farmers in their decision making process regarding their crops. It leverages satellite data complemented by soil data, and takes into account specific regional conditions, cultivation area, and irrigation requirements. The platform proposes crop rotation strategies based on NASA data; it analyzes the current rotation pattern and compares it against two potential three-year alternatives to determine the best course of action. Furthermore, it incorporates the farmer’s own insights regarding potential shifts in climate and temperature over that period. This approach simplifies field management for farmers, as unforeseen changes in weather or temperature can otherwise lead to the loss of a harvest or soil degradation. By transforming satellite data into actionable guidance, StelliFarm, in combination with the farmer’s expertise, helps achieve better agricultural outcomes.
details:
SatelliFarm is a web-based advisor that tells farmers what to plant. The farmer marks their plot on a map of the U.S. and enters its size and what matters most to them (water, income, soil, forage, nitrogen). The server gathers open data from NASA and other sources for that location: climate (POWER), rainfall (GPM-IMERG), soil moisture (SMAP), land surface temperature (ECOSTRESS), slope (SRTM), vegetation (Sentinel-2), actual evapotranspiration (OpenET), plus soil, crop history, yields and prices from the USDA. It fuses the sources and calculates each crop’s water balance (FAO-56 evapotranspiration). It then delivers the recommended crops, the water, climate, pest, soil and market risks, and three 3-year rotation strategies compared with what the farmer does today. It turns scattered technical data into a clear, explained recommendation. It shows how much irrigation and nitrogen fertilizer each option needs, how many months the soil is left bare, and the expected gross income. It is free, available in Spanish and English, works in U.S. or metric units, and every formula is visible to anyone who wants to check it.

Helping farmers adapt to a changing climate (the “Field Shift”): choosing crops and rotations that fit their land and the water they have, using less irrigation and fertilizer, protecting the soil from erosion, and breaking pest cycles. A climate scenario lets them test a drier or hotter future before planting.

NASA data: POWER, GPM-IMERG, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, SRTM and AppEEARS. Other data: Sentinel-2, OpenET, USDA (SSURGO, CDL, NASS, AMS, SCAN), ACIS, ISRIC SoilGrids and the FCC Area API. Software: Python, FastAPI, Google Earth Engine, Leaflet, Chart.js, JavaScript and Vercel.

AI was used to fix programming errors and to automate tasks that do not require engineering judgment; all designs and decisions were made by the team.

It fuses satellite and ground-station data using inverse-variance weighting: the more reliable source carries more weight, and the weights are displayed. It admits what it doesn’t know and lists which sources failed. It compares the farmer’s current rotation (read from satellite crop maps) with two alternatives on a month-by-month timeline, and lets users experiment with climate sliders. It serves two audiences: Farmer mode, in plain language, and Engineer mode, with formulas.

Data quality and uncertainty (each source has a different resolution and error), making sure the farmer can trust and verify the result, the water and nitrogen balance, erosion, pest cycles, income, and the limits of the data (U.S. only, 10 crops, single-point queries). Also cost (free APIs), language and units, and the fact that the tool is a decision aid whose results should be confirmed with local agronomists and extension offices.
